newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Tenaga power tariff hiked by 8.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Tenaga power tariff hiked by 8.3 pct.

text.p: Malaysian utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd is being allowed to raise its power charges by 8.3 percent, Energy, Telecommunications and Posts Minister Leo Moggie said on Wednesday.
The government had agreed to Tenaga raising the power rates by 1.8 cents per unit to 23.5 cents, the minister said.
Moggie told reporters that a Cabinet meeting on Wednesday had decided to allow the tariff increase from May 1.
The hike is close to the eight percent increase many analysts had expected.

"... The government has agreed to allow Tenaga Nasional Bhd to raise electricity tariffs by 1.8 cents per unit, that is from 21.7 cents an average unit now to 23.5 cents an average unit effective from May 1, 1997," the Minister said.
"The 1.8 cents (increase) hopefully is not seen as too much of a burden," Moggie said.
He said the tariff increase was unavoidable because power generation costs have been increasing and were beyond the control of Tenaga as well as Malaysia.
He said the specific breakdown of power rates that will be applicable to various categories of consumers will be announced by Tenaga later.
He said the current tariff levels did not "mirror the true cost of supply borne by Tenaga".
